reason: The sources provide enough factual data to support a short video script with more than 10 fully corroborated claims about ASASSN-15lh.
story: In June 2015, automated telescopes in Chile spotted a dot of light that would shock astronomers. Named ASASSN-15lh, this cosmic explosion shone twenty times brighter than our entire Milky Way galaxy combined, and reached a peak brightness 570 billion times greater than the Sun. Located roughly 3.8 billion light-years away, it radiated more energy in its first fifty days than the Sun will produce in its entire ten-billion-year lifetime. For a time, it was hailed as the most powerful superluminous supernova ever recorded, pushing the theoretical limits of physics. Yet its true nature remains a mystery and heavily disputed. While some scientists argue its unbelievable power came from an ultra-dense, rapidly spinning magnetar, others suggest an even more violent event: a massive, spinning Kerr black hole tearing apart a sun-like star in a rare tidal disruption.
angle: An explosion that shone 570 billion times brighter than the Sun and outshone the entire Milky Way twenty times over.

claims.claim: ASASSN-15lh was discovered in June 2015 by the All Sky Automated Survey for SuperNovae.
At its peak, ASASSN-15lh was 20 times brighter than the combined light of the Milky Way galaxy.
The explosion reached a peak brightness 570 billion times greater than the Sun.
ASASSN-15lh was discovered using twin 14-centimeter telescopes located in Cerro Tololo, Chile.
The event occurred approximately 3.8 to 4 billion light-years away.
The spectrum of ASASSN-15lh was first delivered by the 2.5-meter du Pont Telescope in Chile.
Confirmation of the redshift and distance came from the 10-meter South African Large Telescope.
Unlike typical supernovae found in small star-forming dwarf galaxies, ASASSN-15lh was located in a large, massive galaxy.
The spectrum of ASASSN-15lh lacked hydrogen and helium lines.
One leading explanation is that the explosion was powered by an extremely fast-spinning magnetar.
Another competing explanation is a tidal disruption event caused by a rapidly spinning supermassive Kerr black hole destroying a star.
NASA's Swift space telescope contributed observations to the event.

disputed: Whether the event was actually a superluminous supernova or a tidal disruption event caused by a supermassive black hole. The script should present both possibilities as competing theories among astronomers.
